{{Short description|Genus of silesaurid dinosauromorph}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range = [[Late Triassic]], {{fossilrange|Carnian|Norian|[[Carnian]]–[[Norian]]}} | display_parents = 2 | genus = Rewasaurus | parent_authority = Sen et al., [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | species = minori | authority = Sen et al., 2026 }} '''''Rewasaurus''''' ({{lit|Rewa Basin lizard}}) is an extinct genus of [[dinosauromorph]] allied with taxa traditionally regarded as [[silesaurid]]s (possibly the earliest [[ornithischia]]n dinosaurs). It is known from the [[Late Triassic]] ([[Carnian]] to [[Norian]] age) [[Tiki Formation]] of India. The genus contains a [[monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Rewasaurus minori''''', known from a partial skull. == Discovery and naming == The ''Rewasaurus minori'' holotype material consists of an incomplete skull and articulated [[mandible]] (lower jaw). It is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] at the [[IIT Kharagpur|Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur]] in [[West Bengal]], India, under the code IITKGPR1191. Two isolated partial [[femur|femora]] (thighbones) were also collected from the same formation, but a different locality; while they preserve silesaurid features, they cannot be confidently referred to ''Rewasaurus'' due to the lack of overlapping remains.{{Cite journal |last1=Sen |first1=S. |last2=Basu |first2=P. |last3=Ray |first3=s. |title=First definitive record of a silesaurid (Avemetatarsalia: Dinosauriformes) from the Upper Triassic of India with new insights on its origin and dispersal |year=2026 |journal=The Anatomical Record |doi=10.1002/ar.70366 }} In 2026, Sulagna Sen and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Rewasaurus'' as a new genus and species of silesaurid dinosauriform. The [[generic name (biology)|generic name]], ''Rewasaurus'', refers to the Rewa Basin in [[Madhya Pradesh]], India, from which the fossils were recovered. The [[specific name]], ''minori'', comes from the [[Latin]] word {{lang|la|[[:wikt:minor|minor]]}}, meaning "small." == Description == ''Rewasaurus'' is a small silesaurid, with a reconstructed skull length of ~{{cvt|7|cm|in}}. Sen et al. interpret the only known specimen as belonging to a mature individual based on the fused cranial sutures and well-developed dentition. Like other silesaurids, ''Rewasaurus'' has a relatively slender snout, [[heterodont]] dentition, and a toothless pointed tip of the {{dinogloss|dentary}}. ''Rewasaurus'' can be distinguished from other silesaurids based on the upper dentition being relatively short compared to the lower dentition, the dentary tip lying nearly level with the rest of the tooth-bearing edge, and the {{dinogloss|premaxilla}} bearing at least five teeth. The upper jaw of ''Rewasaurus'' is known only from the partial premaxillae and maxillae with the teeth still in place. A hollow on the upper edge of the premaxilla is probably the narial fossa, which has been damaged due to [[taphonomic]] processes. The maxilla has a straight lower edge continuous with the lower edge of the premaxilla. Small {{dinogloss|nutrient foramina}} line the outer surface of the maxilla, with one per tooth, while two or three foramina are clustered at the tip of the premaxilla. The two bones meet along an angled, interdigitating suture. The edentulous tip of the dentary curves slightly upward, narrowing to a sharp point with an angle of 13° between the upper and lower edges. The bone has no ridge along its outer surface, contrasting with ''[[Diodorus scytobrachion|Diodorus]]'', a possible close relative. Small foramina run irregularly along the bone below the tooth row. == Classification == To test the relationships of ''Rewasaurus'', Sen et al. (2026) inserted it into the [[phylogenetic]] matrices of Dalle-Laste et al. (2025){{Cite journal |last=Dalle-Laste |first=Vitória Z |last2=Garcia |first2=Maurício S |last3=Aureliano |first3=Tito |last4=Ghilardi |first4=Aline M |last5=Kerber |first5=Leonardo |last6=Müller |first6=Rodrigo T |date=2025-08-01 |title=The first allokotosaurian from South America and the Gondwanan radiation of non-archosauriform archosauromorphs |url=https://academic.oup.com/zoolinnean/article/doi/10.1093/zoolinnean/zlaf098/8222032 |journal=Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society |language=en |volume=204 |issue=4 |doi=10.1093/zoolinnean/zlaf098 |issn=1096-3642|url-access=subscription }} and Müller (2025).{{Cite journal |last1=Temp Müller |first1=Rodrigo |date=January 2025 |title=A new "silesaurid" from the oldest dinosauromorph-bearing beds of South America provides insights into the early evolution of bird-line archosaurs |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S1342937X24002764 |journal=[[Gondwana Research]] |volume=137 |pages=13–28 |issue=in press |language=en |doi=10.1016/j.gr.2024.09.007|bibcode=2025GondR.137...13M |url-access=subscription }} The Dalle-Laste et al. (2025) matrix recovered all silesaurids as a [[monophyletic]] clade, although its precise internal relationships could not be determined as many were recovered in an unresolved [[polytomy]]. The Müller (2025) matrix recovered silesaurids as a [[paraphyletic]] grade leading to traditional ornithischians, with ''Rewasaurus'' as a member of the [[Sulcimentisauria]] and the [[sister taxon]] to ''[[Diodorus scytobrachion|Diodorus]]''. The climate during which the Tiki Formation was [[depositional environment|deposited]] is suggested to be [[Semi-arid climate|semi-arid]] with seasonal [[floodplain]]s and [[rainfall]], based on [[palaeosol]]s.{{Cite journal |last1=Ray |first1=Sanghamitra |last2=Bhat |first2=Mohd Safi |last3=Mukherjee |first3=Debarati |last4=Datta |first4=P. M. |date=2016-12-31 |title=Vertebrate fauna from the Late Triassic Tiki Formation of India: new finds and their biostratigraphic implications |url=https://jpsonline.co.in/index.php/jop/article/view/298 |journal=Journal of Palaeosciences |language=en |volume=65 |issue=(1-2) |pages=47–59 |doi=10.54991/jop.2016.298 |issn=2583-4266|doi-access=free }} The formation also has reports of numerous vertebrates like [[phytosaurs]] (such as ''[[Volcanosuchus]]'', ''[[Parasuchus]]'', and ''[[Colossosuchus]]''), dinosaurs (such as indeterminate [[sauropodomorphs]], [[theropods]], and [[herrerasaur]]s), [[rhynchosaurs]] like ''[[Hyperodapedon]]'', [[pseudosuchia]]ns like ''[[Tikisuchus]]'', indeterminate remains belonging to these clades, and various other [[reptile]]s, [[cynodonts]], [[temnospondyls]], [[cartilaginous fish]], and [[ray-finned fishes]]. == References == {{reflist}} {{Avemetatarsalia|D.}} {{Taxonbar|from1=Q141746435}} [[Category:Silesauridae]] [[Category:Monotypic prehistoric reptile genera]] [[Category:Carnian reptiles]] [[Category:Norian reptiles]] [[Category:Fossil taxa described in 2026]] [[Category:Reptiles of India]]
